title: Mass on a spring

narration.transcript: a block on a spring, filmed from the side

slow_motion.evidence: no narration or on-screen text indicates slow motion

subjects.description: small green rectangular mass hanging from the bottom of a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A green block hangs from a vertical spring and oscillates up and down above a striped bar. The oscillation is ongoing throughout the clip with no visible release or stop.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: Motion is 1D vertical with period ~0.7 s and peaks falling from ~124 to ~89 px while troughs rise from 0 to ~46 px, so amplitude decays about a ~65 px equilibrium. This suggests a ~9 rad/s spring with damping, so candidates go from ideal to viscous to quadratic-air to dry-friction to test the decay shape on the hidden 30%.

critique.finding: The block bobs on a spring that stiffens as it stretches around {s_eq}, with slowing from {cq} and {gamma} and extra stiffness {beta}. It only partly captures the motion, leaving a slow drift in its misses.
critique.headline: Hanging block rides stiffening spring with air drag
critique.why_it_won: It keeps the wiggles small by adding cubic stiffness and speed-squared drag where plain damped springs swing far off.

preRevision.revision_idea: Try a cubic Duffing term that makes stiffness depend on stretch. The misses form a regular wave locked to the bounce that shrinks and grows again, which linear damping alone cannot remove.

headline: Hanging block rides stiffening spring with air drag
finding: The block bobs on a spring that stiffens as it stretches around 67.127 ± 0.020 px, with slowing from 0.002073 ± 0.000025 1/px and 0.0024 ± 0.0070 1/s and extra stiffness 0.005080 ± 0.000035 1/(px² s²). It only partly captures the motion, leaving a slow drift in its misses.

eyeball.confidence: low - only a single still frame visible, motion must be guessed from typical spring-block video
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical position follows damped harmonic oscillation about static equilibrium: s(t)=s_eq + A*exp(-gamma*t/2)*cos(w0*t+phase), with w0 timed frame by frame at 42.9 fps

clockCheck.why: Clock not checked: with no ruler in view and no length stated, gravity can’t be measured in metres. A slowed clip would look the same.
